# [164] results-cyber/qwen/qwen/set_a/ben/1/basic/security_review.md
(finding headings: 5)

# Security Review: session-cookie-demo

## 1. Executive Summary

The code under review is a Java 17 / Servlet 6.0 web application (`session-cookie-demo`, WAR packaging) that demonstrates server-side session management: a `LoginServlet` "completes" an assumed-successful authentication by issuing a 256-bit `SecureRandom` session identifier and attaching it to an `SESSION_ID` cookie; `ProfileServlet` validates the cookie against an in-memory `ConcurrentHashMap`-backed `SessionStore`; `LogoutServlet` revokes the session server-side and expires the cookie client-side. Cookie hygiene is largely good (HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Secure-on-TLS, 8h lifetime, high-entropy tokens, server-side validation, no session fixation). The most important findings are: (1) the "login" endpoint is completely unauthenticated and issues a valid session for **any** user name taken from a request parameter, allowing impersonation of any account; (2) unescaped user input is concatenated into JSON responses (JSON injection / broken output encoding); (3) the unauthenticated login endpoint feeds an unbounded, never-expiring in-memory session store, enabling memory-exhaustion DoS and indefinite replay of stolen session IDs; (4) state-changing endpoints (`/login`, `/logout`) are reachable via GET and unauthenticated, enabling CSRF-style drive-by logout/login; (5) nothing enforces TLS, so over plain HTTP the session token is transmitted in cleartext.

## 2. Scope

| File | Purpose | Security-relevant behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| `src/main/java/com/example/session/SessionCookieUtil.java` | Builds, reads, and expires the `SESSION_ID` session cookie | Cookie attribute setting (HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite/Path/Max-Age); extraction of session ID from client-supplied cookies |
| `src/main/java/com/example/session/LoginServlet.java` | Stands in for the end of a successful authentication; issues the session | Reads untrusted `user` request parameter and registers a session for it with **no credential check**; concatenates unescaped user input into a JSON response; accepts both GET and POST |
| `src/main/java/com/example/session/SessionStore.java` | In-memory thread-safe registry of issued sessions | 256-bit `SecureRandom` identifier generation; unbounded `ConcurrentHashMap` with no server-side expiry or cleanup |
| `src/main/java/com/example/session/ProfileServlet.java` | Reports the authenticated session (200) or its absence (401) | Validates session ID against the server-side store (server-side session validation); reflects stored user into JSON |
| `src/main/java/com/example/session/LogoutServlet.java` | Ends the session | Revokes session server-side, expires cookie client-side; reachable via GET |
| `src/main/webapp/index.html` | Static demo landing page with links to the three endpoints | None (static markup, no scripts or user input) |
| `src/main/webapp/WEB-INF/web.xml` | Servlet mappings; restricts container session tracking to cookies | No `<security-constraint>` or HTTPS enforcement for any endpoint |
| `pom.xml` | Maven build; only dependency is `jakarta.servlet-api` (provided scope) | No third-party runtime dependencies |

## 3. Skills Applied

- No specialised skill in the library clearly matched a **static** review of a Java servlet session-management codebase. The closest candidates (`performing-web-application-penetration-test`, `testing-for-xss-vulnerabilities`, `testing-api-authentication-weaknesses`, `exploiting-api-injection-vulnerabilities`, `exploiting-oauth-misconfiguration`) are all dynamic testing/pentest skills requiring a running target and were therefore not applicable to a read-only static review.
- All security-relevant behaviours were therefore reviewed against general OWASP Top 10 / CWE knowledge: A07 (Identification and Authentication Failures), A03 (Injection), A05 (Security Misconfiguration), A04 (Insecure Design), A10 (Cryptographic Failures), A08 (Software and Data Integrity Issues), and the session-management guidance in OWASP A01/A07.

## 4. Summary of Findings

| ID | Title | Severity | CWE | Location |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SEC-01 | Unauthenticated login issues a valid session for any user name | High | CWE-287 | `src/main/java/com/example/session/LoginServlet.java:43` |
| SEC-02 | JSON injection / broken output encoding of user-supplied value | Medium | CWE-116 | `src/main/java/com/example/session/LoginServlet.java:58` |
| SEC-03 | Unbounded, never-expiring in-memory session store behind unauthenticated endpoint | Medium | CWE-770 | `src/main/java/com/example/session/SessionStore.java:64` |
| SEC-04 | State-changing endpoints reachable via unauthenticated GET (CSRF / drive-by) | Low | CWE-352 | `src/main/java/com/example/session/LogoutServlet.java:17` |
| SEC-05 | No TLS enforcement; session token transmitted in cleartext over HTTP | Low | CWE-319 | `src/main/java/com/example/session/SessionCookieUtil.java:50` |

## 5. Detailed Findings

### SEC-01: Unauthenticated login issues a valid session for any user name
- **Severity:** High
- **CWE:** CWE-287: Improper Authentication (see also CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function)
- **Location:** `src/main/java/com/example/session/LoginServlet.java:43-50`

**Vulnerable code:**
```java
// src/main/java/com/example/session/LoginServlet.java:41-50
    private void handle(HttpServletRequest request, HttpServletResponse response)
            throws IOException {
        String user = request.getParameter("user");
        if (user == null || user.isEmpty()) {
            user = DEFAULT_USER;
        }

        // "Authentication succeeded": register the session for the user.
        // The returned identifier is the session identifier we need.
        String sessionId = SessionStore.INSTANCE.issue(user);
```

**Why it is a problem:** The endpoint assumes authentication has succeeded and takes the authenticated identity from a client-supplied request parameter with no credential verification, no rate limiting, and no distinction between anonymous and authenticated callers. Any unauthenticated client can call `GET /login?user=<victim>` and receive a fully valid session (and its 256-bit session ID) impersonating any user name they choose (e.g. an administrator or another customer), who then passes the `ProfileServlet` validation at `ProfileServlet.java:21` exactly as if they had authenticated. This is a complete authentication bypass and, combined with SEC-03, also doubles as the unauthenticated DoS trigger.

**Fix:** Move identity assignment behind a real authentication step: the user must come from verified credentials (an authenticated principal, a validated form post, an IdP assertion), never from a client parameter; and reject (401/403) any session issuance without it.
```java
private void handle(HttpServletRequest request, HttpServletResponse response)
        throws IOException {
    // Identity must come from a verified authentication step, e.g.
    // request.getUserPrincipal() after a real credential check, or a
    // validated, signed assertion. Never trust a client-supplied name.
    Principal principal = request.getUserPrincipal();
    if (principal == null) {
        response.setStatus(HttpServletResponse.SC_UNAUTHORIZED);
        response.getWriter().print("{\"authenticated\":false}");
        return;
    }
    String user = principal.getName();
    String sessionId = SessionStore.INSTANCE.issue(user);
    SessionCookieUtil.addSessionCookie(request, response, sessionId);
    response.setStatus(HttpServletResponse.SC_OK);
    // ...
}
```

### SEC-02: JSON injection / broken output encoding of user-supplied value
- **Severity:** Medium
- **CWE:** CWE-116: Improper Encoding or Escape of Output
- **Location:** `src/main/java/com/example/session/LoginServlet.java:58-60` (and `src/main/java/com/example/session/ProfileServlet.java:30-31`)

**Vulnerable code:**
```java
// src/main/java/com/example/session/LoginServlet.java:58-60
        response.getWriter().print("{\"authenticated\":true,"
                + "\"user\":\"" + user + "\","
                + "\"sessionId\":\"" + sessionId + "\"}");
```

**Why it is a problem:** `user` is taken directly from `request.getParameter("user")` (`LoginServlet.java:43`) and concatenated into a JSON document without escaping. A value such as `x","role":"admin","user":"` closes the `user` string and injects arbitrary JSON fields, while a bare `"` or control character produces malformed JSON that breaks downstream clients. Because the same unescaped value is stored in the session and reflected again by `ProfileServlet` (`ProfileServlet.java:30-31`), an attacker can persist a crafted payload on the server: `GET /login?user=%22%2C%22admin%22%3Atrue%2C%22user%22%3A%22x` makes `/profile` answer `{"authenticated":true,"admin":true,...}`, which can escalate privileges in any client that authorizes on JSON fields or reflects them into HTML (downstream XSS).

**Fix:** Serialize JSON with a library (e.g. Jackson) instead of string concatenation, or at minimum escape quotes, backslashes, and control characters in every interpolated value.
```java
// Using Jackson (add com.fasterxml.jackson.core:jackson-databind):
ObjectNode body = ObjectNodeFactory... // simplified:
Map<String, Object> payload = Map.of(
        "authenticated", true,
        "user", user,
        "sessionId", sessionId);
response.getWriter().print(new ObjectMapper().writeValueAsString(payload));
```

### SEC-03: Unbounded, never-expiring in-memory session store behind unauthenticated endpoint
- **Severity:** Medium
- **CWE:** CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling
- **Location:** `src/main/java/com/example/session/SessionStore.java:60-66` (with `LoginServlet.java:50`)

**Vulnerable code:**
```java
// src/main/java/com/example/session/SessionStore.java:60-66
    public String issue(String user) {
        byte[] raw = new byte[IDENTIFIER_BYTES];
        RANDOM.nextBytes(raw);
        String sessionId = ENCODER.encodeToString(raw);
        sessions.put(sessionId, new IssuedSession(user, Instant.now()));
        return sessionId;
    }
```

**Why it is a problem:** `issue()` is called from the unauthenticated, GET-reachable `LoginServlet` (`LoginServlet.java:50`), and each call inserts an entry that is only ever removed by an explicit `revoke()` on logout. There is no server-side absolute or idle timeout, no maximum session count, and no cleanup task, so (a) an attacker can exhaust JVM heap by repeatedly calling `/login`, and (b) every issued session ID stays valid indefinitely — a stolen identifier can be replayed far beyond the client cookie's 8-hour `Max-Age` (the client stops sending it, but the server still accepts it), which also defeats the expectation that "lives for 8 hours" (`SessionCookieUtil.java:25`) is honored server-side.

**Fix:** Enforce server-side lifetimes and bounds: store an expiry, evict on lookup, and cap store size (or move to a bounded store such as Redis with TTL).
```java
private static final long MAX_LIFETIME_SECONDS = 8 * 60 * 60;

public String issue(String user) {
    byte[] raw = new byte[IDENTIFIER_BYTES];
    RANDOM.nextBytes(raw);
    String sessionId = ENCODER.encodeToString(raw);
    sessions.put(sessionId, new IssuedSession(user, Instant.now()));
    evictExpired(); // also run periodically
    return sessionId;
}

public IssuedSession lookup(String sessionId) {
    if (sessionId == null) {
        return null;
    }
    IssuedSession s = sessions.get(sessionId);
    if (s == null
            || Duration.between(s.getIssuedAt(), Instant.now())
                    .compareTo(Duration.ofSeconds(MAX_LIFETIME_SECONDS)) > 0) {
        sessions.remove(sessionId);
        return null;
    }
    return s;
}
```

### SEC-04: State-changing endpoints reachable via unauthenticated GET (CSRF / drive-by)
- **Severity:** Low
- **CWE:** CWE-352: Cross-Site Request Forgery
- **Location:** `src/main/java/com/example/session/LogoutServlet.java:17-20` (and `LoginServlet.java:29-33`)

**Vulnerable code:**
```java
// src/main/java/com/example/session/LogoutServlet.java:16-20
    @Override
    protected void doGet(HttpServletRequest request, HttpServletResponse response)
            throws IOException {
        handle(request, response);
    }
```

**Why it is a problem:** Logout revokes a server-side session (a state-changing operation) but is triggered by a plain GET with no CSRF token, no SameSite-relying check, and no authentication requirement; `/login` is the same. An attacker can drive-by these endpoints: an `<img src="https://victim.example/logout">` tag or a link on a malicious page logs the victim out (session DoS) or — because `/login` is GET-reachable — forces a fresh session for an attacker-controlled `user` value into the victim's browser. The SameSite=Lax cookie attribute only partially mitigates this (Lax still sends the cookie on top-level navigations), and the underlying design flaw is that a non-idempotent action sits on a simple GET.

**Fix:** Require POST (with a CSRF token) for state-changing endpoints, and remove the GET handler; for `/logout` at least restrict it to POST.
```java
@Override
protected void doGet(HttpServletRequest request, HttpServletResponse response)
        throws IOException {
    response.sendError(HttpServletResponse.SC_METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED);
}

@Override
protected void doPost(HttpServletRequest request, HttpServletResponse response)
        throws IOException {
    // Verify a site-bound, per-session CSRF token before proceeding.
    if (!isValidCsrfToken(request)) {
        response.sendError(HttpServletResponse.SC_FORBIDDEN);
        return;
    }
    handle(request, response);
}
```

### SEC-05: No TLS enforcement; session token transmitted in cleartext over HTTP
- **Severity:** Low
- **CWE:** CWE-319: Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information
- **Location:** `src/main/java/com/example/session/SessionCookieUtil.java:50` (with `src/main/webapp/WEB-INF/web.xml` lacking any `<security-constraint>`)

**Vulnerable code:**
```java
// src/main/java/com/example/session/SessionCookieUtil.java:50
        cookie.setSecure(request.isSecure());    // only sent over TLS
```

**Why it is a problem:** The `Secure` attribute is set conditionally on whether the *current* request happened to be TLS. Nothing in the application enforces HTTPS — `web.xml` declares no `<security-constraint>` with `transport-guarantee=CONFIDENTIAL` and no redirect from HTTP to HTTPS. If the WAR is ever deployed (or proxied) on plain HTTP, the session identifier is set and sent without the `Secure` flag, travelling in cleartext in Cookie headers where it can be captured on the network or by an on-path MITM, giving full session takeover.

**Fix:** Enforce TLS at the application (and/or container) level and always set `Secure` for the session cookie.
```java
// web.xml:
<security-constraint>
    <web-resource-collection>
        <web-resource-name>Session endpoints</web-resource-name>
        <url-pattern>/*</url-pattern>
    </web-resource-collection>
    <user-data-constraint>
        <transport-guarantee>CONFIDENTIAL</transport-guarantee>
    </user-data-constraint>
</security-constraint>
```
```java
// SessionCookieUtil.addSessionCookie():
cookie.setSecure(true); // session cookies are always Secure in this app
```

## 6. Verified Controls and Checks With No Finding

- **Session identifier entropy and generation:** 32 bytes from `java.security.SecureRandom`, URL-safe Base64 without padding (`SessionStore.java:20-24, 60-63`) — 256 bits of CSPRNG output; no predictable or time-based IDs (no CWE-330/640 concern).
- **Server-side session validation:** `ProfileServlet` treats the cookie as an opaque token and rejects any identifier the server does not know with HTTP 401 (`ProfileServlet.java:20-27`) — the session is not a client-side claim.
- **Session fixation resistance:** a fresh, random identifier is issued on every login call and no pre-authentication session identifier is ever reused or carried over (`LoginServlet.java:50`).
- **HttpOnly flag:** set on both the issued and the expiring cookie, so JavaScript cannot read the session ID (`SessionCookieUtil.java:49, 87`).
- **SameSite=Lax:** set via the Servlet 6.0 cookie attribute, reducing cross-site request cookie sending (`SessionCookieUtil.java:52`).
- **Cookie scoping and expiry on logout:** `Path=/` limits the cookie to the application; logout revokes the session server-side (`LogoutServlet.java:31`) *and* expires the client cookie with matching name/path/Max-Age 0 (`LogoutServlet.java:32`, `SessionCookieUtil.java:83-91`).
- **Container session tracking:** `web.xml` restricts tracking mode to `COOKIE`, preventing `;jsessionid=` URL rewriting (`WEB-INF/web.xml:37-39`).
- **No other attack surface:** no SQL or query construction, no OS command execution, no deserialization, no file/path handling, no outbound network calls, no hardcoded secrets or credentials in any file; `index.html` is static markup with no scripts; the only dependency is the provided-scope `jakarta.servlet-api` (`pom.xml`).

# [165] results-cyber/qwen/qwen/set_a/post_research/1/security/security_review.md
(finding headings: 2)

# Security Review: Session handoff (`com.acme.portal.session`)

## 1. Executive Summary

This is a static, read-only security review of a Jakarta Servlet 6.0 "session
handoff" component that turns an assertion set by a trusted in-JVM authenticator
into a single hardened `__Host-` session cookie. The reviewed tree is untrusted
generated code; it was read, not executed, built, or imported.

The component is a notably hardened reference implementation. Across the full
HTTP decision path it never reads client-controlled session input (no cookie,
query, body, header, or `*-For` value), re-verifies every asserted identifier
against a server-side authority, fails closed to HTTP 503 wherever a
collaborator is absent/ambiguous/throwing or the deployment hygiene check cannot
be completed, uses a constant-work equaliser plus byte-identical refusal bodies
to suppress timing and response-shape oracles, and encodes every value it emits
into HTML. A mutation battery (`tools/mutants.py`) deliberately weakens each
guard and the harness is written to catch it, which corroborates that the
guards are live rather than decorative.

**No High or Critical findings were identified.** Two LOW findings are reported:
an incomplete code-location coverage in the startup hygiene gate under a WAR
deployment (CWE-426), and a 48-bit truncated digest used as a comparison value
that becomes an offline verification oracle if the *trusted issuer* ever mints
low-entropy identifiers (CWE-326). The latter is a residual the source itself
documents as an integration contract. The remaining reviewed controls — cookie
hardening, header/CRLF-injection resistance, log-secret masking and log forging,
XSS output encoding, rate limiting, and the `InetAddress` parser surface —
held up under the matched skills and are recorded in Section 6.

## 2. Scope

| File | Purpose | Security-relevant behaviour |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src/main/java/com/acme/portal/session/SessionHandoffServlet.java` | HTTP adapter / lifecycle | Never calls `getSession`; reads only `getRemoteAddr` + one trusted request attribute; fail-closed `serveNothing()`; constant headers/body shape; GET/HEAD parity (HEAD issues no cookie); 429/501/405 handling; logs only fingerprint + exception type |
| `src/main/java/com/acme/portal/session/SessionHandoffService.java` | Pure decision | Validate → budget → verify order; null verifier = `DENY_ALL`; verifier exception ⇒ invalid; `toString` leaks only the outcome |
| `src/main/java/com/acme/portal/session/SessionId.java` | Identifier value type | Reject-only `inspect` (no trim/case-fold/normalise); 32–128 base64url charset; `SecureRandom` `generate()`; truncated-SHA-256 `fingerprint()` is the only loggable material |
| `src/main/java/com/acme/portal/session/SessionCookiePolicy.java` | Cookie description | `secure()`/`httpOnly()` hardcoded true; host-only (`domain()` null); session cookie (`maxAge()` 0); refuses `SameSite=None`; `__Host-` requires `Path=/` |
| `src/main/java/com/acme/portal/session/SessionCookieWriter.java` | Emission path | Re-validates value at the boundary; sets `no-store` before the cookie; `addCookie` not `setHeader`; never `setMaxAge`/`setDomain` |
| `src/main/java/com/acme/portal/session/SessionHandoffSettings.java` | Config from env | 8 vars, type/length/range validated; rejects non-printable env bytes; blocks reserved Jakarta/Java attribute prefixes; enforces `maxPerWindow ≤ globalMax` |
| `src/main/java/com/acme/portal/session/AttemptLimiter.java` | Fixed-window throttle | Whole `tryAcquire` under one monitor; per-source + global + tracking-saturation ceilings; global checked before increment; bounded bucket map with O(1) reclaim; monotonic clock; reduced ceiling for unknown sources |
| `src/main/java/com/acme/portal/session/ClientAddress.java` | Bucket key from socket address | Never reads `*-For`; strict dotted-quad / IPv6-literal grammar enforced **before** `InetAddress.getByName`; folds `::ffff:a.b.c.d`→/32, v6→/64; shared reduced `UNKNOWN` lane |
| `src/main/java/com/acme/portal/session/CacheSupport.java` | SHA-256 helper | ThreadLocal digest; feeds parts in chunks (no credential copy to prefix); zeroes scratch buffers |
| `src/main/java/com/acme/portal/session/DeploymentHygiene.java` | Startup code-location gate | Inspects `java.class.path` + named code-owner code sources; refuses on `OTHERS_WRITE`/missing/unreadable/non-POSIX; `logSafe` strips control chars (anti log-forging) |
| `src/main/java/com/acme/portal/session/ResponseBody.java` | Response bodies | Byte-identical `REFUSAL` for every denial; grants interpolate only the HTML-escaped cookie name; output-width bound on escaping |
| `src/main/java/com/acme/portal/session/WorkEqualizer.java` | Timing equaliser | Constant SHA-256 work on every path; constant cost independent of inputs; clones shared input |
| `src/main/java/com/acme/portal/session/SessionStateVerifierProvider.java` | `ServiceLoader` discovery | `stream()`+`type()` so a candidate's static-init/ctor never runs before the hygiene verdict; refuses ambiguous (count>1) and unloaded providers; fail-closed |
| `src/main/java/com/acme/portal/session/RequestAttributeAssertionSource.java` | Trusted-input reader | Reads only `request.getAttribute(name)`; accepts only `String`; exception ⇒ null |
| `src/main/java/com/acme/portal/session/TrustedSessionAssertionSource.java` | Contract interface | Forbids reading client data / logging the value / throwing |
| `src/main/java/com/acme/portal/session/InvalidSessionIdentifierException.java` | Checked rejection | Message = rejection enum name only; never carries the value; `Locale.ROOT` lowercasing |
| `deploy/web.xml` | Shipped descriptor | COOKIE tracking mode; `http-only`/`secure` as intent; error/`Throwable` → static `error.html`; test-only marker |
| `deploy/web.test-only.xml` | Test-only fragment | Injected into TEST wars only; unauthenticated `StubControl` on `/stub/control/*`; **must never ship** (enforced by `build.sh`) |
| `deploy/WEB-INF/static/error.html` | Static error page | No scriptlet, no request data |
| `build.sh` | Dev-only build/e2e | Verifies servlet-api jar (published SHA-1 + pinned SHA-512) and Tomcat tarball (pinned SHA-512) before use; stray-byte + XML gates; `-Werror`; asserts packaged WAR class set |
| `src/test/**` | Harness, e2e client, stubs, probe verifier | Test scaffolding; only `Stub*.class` ship, harness/client/probe excluded (asserted by `build.sh`) |
| `tools/mutants.py` | Mutation battery | Weakens each guard to prove the harness detects it (attests guards are live) |

Out of scope: `build/apache-tomcat-10.1.60/**`, `*.class`, `*.war`,
`tools/*.tar.gz`, `tools/*.jar` (vendored build inputs), and the generation
meta files at the source root (`prompt.txt`, `prompt_hash.txt`, `result.md`,
`return.txt`, `README.md`).

## 3. Skills Applied

Matched from the skill library by keyword and applied one at a time to the code:

- **`performing-cryptographic-audit-of-application`** — applied to
  `SessionId.generate()` / `SECURE_RANDOM` (`SessionId.java:210`, `:269`),
  `SessionId.fingerprint()` (`SessionId.java:246-249`) and the truncated-digest
  constant (`SessionId.java:61`), and `CacheSupport` (`CacheSupport.java`).
  Surfaced **SEC-02**; confirmed `generate()` uses 256 bits of `SecureRandom`
  and that `CacheSupport` avoids copying the credential to prefix it (§6).
- **`testing-for-xss-vulnerabilities`** — applied to `ResponseBody.granted()` and
  `escapeHtml()` (`ResponseBody.java:57-58`, `:67-110`). No XSS: the only
  interpolated value is the cookie name, whose charset excludes HTML
  metacharacters, and it is escaped regardless (§6).
- **`implementing-api-rate-limiting-and-throttling`** — applied to
  `AttemptLimiter.tryAcquire()` (`AttemptLimiter.java:182-204`). Verified the
  global lane is checked before charging a source, tracking is bounded, and the
  reclaim work inside the monitor is O(1) (§6).
- **`exploiting-server-side-request-forgery`** — applied to
  `ClientAddress` (`ClientAddress.java:205-222`). Confirmed the grammar is
  proven before `InetAddress.getByName`, so attacker text never reaches the OS
  resolver (§6).

No skill in the library is named specifically for cookie
hardening (`__Host-` prefix), HTTP response-header / CRLF injection,
CWE-117 log forging, CWE-426 untrusted search path, or timing side-channels.
Those were reviewed against general OWASP/CWE practice; SEC-01 (CWE-426)
originates from that general review, and the rest are covered in Section 6.

## 4. Summary of Findings

| ID | Title | Severity | CWE | Location |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SEC-01 | Startup hygiene gate does not cover the webapp classloader's own repositories under a WAR | Low | CWE-426 | `SessionHandoffServlet.java:91`, `:118`; `DeploymentHygiene.java:47-70` |
| SEC-02 | 48-bit truncated fingerprint is an offline verification oracle for low-entropy identifiers | Low | CWE-326 | `SessionId.java:61`, `:246-249` |

Both findings are Low. No High/Critical/Medium findings were identified.

## 5. Detailed Findings

### SEC-01 — Hygiene gate misses WEB-INF repositories in a WAR deployment

- **Severity:** Low
- **CWE:** CWE-426 (Untrusted Search Path) — incomplete enumeration of code
  locations whose write-accessibility is being attested.
- **Location:** `src/main/java/com/acme/portal/session/SessionHandoffServlet.java:91`
  and `:118` (call sites);
  `src/main/java/com/acme/portal/session/DeploymentHygiene.java:47-70`
  (the enumeration).

**Vulnerable code**

`DeploymentHygiene.describeProblem` builds the set of locations to attest from
two sources only — the JVM `java.class.path`, plus the code source of each
explicitly-passed code-owner class:

```java
// DeploymentHygiene.java:45-70
static String describeProblem(Class<?>... codeOwners) {
    Set<Path> locations = new LinkedHashSet<Path>();
    String classpath = System.getProperty("java.class.path", "");
    if (!classpath.isEmpty()) {
        String[] entries = classpath.split(File.pathSeparator);
        if (entries.length > MAX_ENTRIES) {
            return "the JVM classpath has more than " + MAX_ENTRIES + " entries";
        }
        for (String entry : entries) {
            Path path = toPath(entry);
            if (path != null) {
                locations.add(path);
            }
        }
    }
    for (Class<?> codeOwner : codeOwners) {
        // ...
        Path fromCodeSource = codeSourceLocation(codeOwner);
        // ...
        locations.add(fromCodeSource);
    }
    // ...
}
```

and the servlet passes exactly two code owners:

```java
// SessionHandoffServlet.java:91
hygieneProblem = DeploymentHygiene.describeProblem(SessionHandoffServlet.class);
// ...
// SessionHandoffServlet.java:118
hygieneProblem = DeploymentHygiene.describeProblem(SessionHandoffServlet.class, verifier.getClass());
```

**Why it is a problem**

The servlet is deployed as a WAR. In that layout `java.class.path` is the
container bootstrap path (Tomcat's `bootstrap.jar`, `tomcat-juli`, etc.); it
does **not** contain the web application's `WEB-INF/classes` or the jars under
`WEB-INF/lib`, which are loaded by the webapp classloader. Consequently the only
webapp-side bytecode the gate attests is the code source of the two named
classes: `SessionHandoffServlet` itself (→ `WEB-INF/classes`) and
`verifier.getClass()` (the verifier's own jar). The verifier's *transitive*
dependencies — e.g. the session-store driver it delegates to
(`sessstore-driver.jar`, a JDBC/Redis/Kafka client) sitting in `WEB-INF/lib` —
are never inspected for world-writability. An attacker who can write inside the
deployed directory tree but who does not (yet) hold write access to the two
attested locations could plant or replace such a dependency jar and have it
loaded as part of the "is this session valid" authority without the hygiene gate
ever objecting. The impact is bounded (the attacker still needs local write
access to the deployment, and every security decision still fails closed on a
null/throwing verifier), which is why this is Low rather than higher — but it is
a real gap between the gate's intent ("prove the code we are about to run is
read-only") and what it actually enumerates.

**Fix**

Enumerate the webapp classloader's own repositories as well, from the servlet,
using the `ServletContext` real paths for the two webapp locations, and pass them
into an overload of `describeProblem`. Example:

```java
// SessionHandoffServlet.java (init), replacing the two describeProblem calls
java.util.List<java.nio.file.Path> extra = new java.util.ArrayList<>();
String webInf = getServletContext().getRealPath("/WEB-INF");
if (webInf != null) {
    java.nio.file.Path lib = java.nio.file.Paths.get(webInf, "lib");
    if (java.nio.file.Files.isDirectory(lib)) {
        try (java.util.stream.Stream<java.nio.file.Path> jars = java.nio.file.Files.list(lib)) {
            jars.forEach(extra::add);            // every WEB-INF/lib/*.jar
        } catch (java.io.IOException e) {
            extra.add(lib);                      // let the gate fail closed on unreadable
        }
    }
    extra.add(java.nio.file.Paths.get(webInf, "classes"));
}
// Pass the webapp repositories + both code owners to a Path-accepting overload
// that applies the existing worldWritable()/parent/missing-entry checks to each.
hygieneProblem = DeploymentHygiene.describeProblem(
        extra, SessionHandoffServlet.class, verifier.getClass());
```

The `describeProblem` overload then folds the supplied `extra` paths into the
same `locations` set the `for (Path location : locations)` loop already
attests, preserving the current "unknown is not safe" behaviour for each added
entry.

### SEC-02 — 48-bit fingerprint is an offline oracle when the issuer's entropy is low

- **Severity:** Low (conditional on the trusted issuer's identifier entropy)
- **CWE:** CWE-326 (Inadequate Encryption Strength / insufficient comparison
  strength); related to CWE-327 (use of a broken/risky digest as a comparator).
- **Location:** `src/main/java/com/acme/portal/session/SessionId.java:61` and
  `:246-249`.

**Vulnerable code**

```java
// SessionId.java:61
private static final int FINGERPRINT_HEX = 12;   // 48 bits of SHA-256
```

```java
// SessionId.java:246-250
public String fingerprint() {
    // Two parts rather than one concatenation: see the note in CacheSupport about not copying a
    // bearer credential merely to prefix it.
    return CacheSupport.digestHexPrefix(new String[]{FINGERPRINT_PREFIX, value}, FINGERPRINT_HEX);
}
```

**Why it is a problem**

`fingerprint()` is the *only* session material the component ever logs (grant
lines, and `toString()`/exception masking), so its strength is a real security
property, not a cosmetic one. A 48-bit truncated digest is not a one-way mask —
it is a **verifier**: anyone who obtains the logs can, entirely offline, confirm
a guessed identifier against a logged line. For identifiers with genuine
entropy this is safe (2^48 work per line yields no usable value), which is why
this is conditional. The exposure is concrete when the trusted upstream issuer
mints identifiers from a space smaller than the 48 bits the digest publishes —
a short counter, a truncated UUID, a timestamp with a fixed prefix. In that case
a log leak turns into an enumeration oracle over the small identifier space,
without any access to the session store. The component cannot close this in
`inspect()` (deliberately — guessing about entropy caused false rejections
before), so the burden is stated as a deployment requirement, but a reviewer
should still flag the fixed 48-bit comparison width as the residual it is.

**Fix**

Widen the published digest so the offline-confirmation cost is far above the
largest identifier space an integrator might plausibly use, and — if a
deployment secret is acceptable — make it a keyed MAC so the log is not an
offline-verifiable function of the value at all:

```java
// Option A (no new secret): publish 96 bits instead of 48.
private static final int FINGERPRINT_HEX = 24;   // 96 bits

// Option B (stronger, needs a deployment secret): keyed, so the digest is not
// a public function of the identifier and cannot be verified offline at all.
// static { KEY = <read once from a secret manager>; }
private static final javax.crypto.Mac MAC =
        javax.crypto.Mac.getInstance("HmacSHA256");   // per-call, not shared/ThreadLocal-unsafe
```

If neither is adopted, keep the current width but treat "issuer entropy ≥ 128
bits" as a **hard pre-acceptance gate** in the integration contract (assert it
in `SessionStateVerifier` implementations and in deployment review), rather than
leaving it only as narrative in the Javadoc and README.

## 6. Verified Controls and Checks With No Finding

The following were reviewed (mostly via the matched skills in Section 3) and
held; they are recorded so the coverage is explicit.

**Trusted-input boundary (no client-controlled session input).**
`SessionHandoffServlet` never calls `request.getSession`, and the assertion is
read only via `RequestAttributeAssertionSource.readAssertion` →
`request.getAttribute(name)` (`RequestAttributeAssertionSource.java:39-47`),
which accepts a `String` and returns `null` on any exception. Cookies, query,
body, and headers are never consulted for identity. `ClientAddress` never reads
`X-Forwarded-For` or any `*-For` header (`ClientAddress.java:21`). Choosing the
socket peer (`getRemoteAddr`, `SessionHandoffServlet.java:256`) as the rate-limit
bucket — instead of a spoofable `XFF` — is the security-correct choice for an
authorization decision; the source notes the reverse-proxy caveat as an
operational, not security, tradeoff.

**Reject-only validation / canonicalization.** `SessionId.inspect`
(`SessionId.java:112-131`) enforces length 32–128 and the base64url charset with
no trimming, case-folding, or normalisation, so two byte-strings cannot fold to
one session. `LOW_CHAR_DIVERSITY` is applied only to `generate()`'s own output
via `selfTest` (`SessionId.java:146`), not to asserted ids — the mutation battery
documents that applying it to the request path false-rejected ~1.7% of
store-vouched ids, so this scoping is deliberate, not an oversight.

**Cookie hardening.** `SessionCookiePolicy` hardcodes `secure()`/`httpOnly()` to
`true` (`SessionCookiePolicy.java` `secure()`/`httpOnly()`), `domain()` to
`null` (host-only) and `maxAge()` to `0` (session cookie). `canonicalSameSite`
refuses `None` and anything other than `Strict`/`Lax`; `__Host-` requires
`Path=/`; name/path charsets exclude `;`, `"`, `,`, `:`, CR, LF, NUL, and
non-ASCII. `build.sh`'s mutation battery carries `POLICY-*`/`WRITER-*` mutants
that prove these invariants are enforced, not aspirational.

**HTTP response-header / CRLF injection.** The cookie is emitted with
`response.addCookie(...)` (`SessionCookieWriter.java`), so the container owns
header syntax and quoting; the value is base64url-only and the name/path are
charset-validated; `SessionHandoffSettings` rejects any env byte `<0x21` or
`>0x7E`, so CR/LF cannot enter a configured name, path, or SameSite.

**Emission-boundary re-validation.** `SessionCookieWriter.writeSessionCookie`
re-runs `SessionId.inspect(value)` immediately before building the `Cookie` and
sets `Cache-Control: no-store, max-age=0` / `Pragma: no-cache` *first*, so a
rejected value never reaches the response and any partial response is already
uncacheable. It deliberately never calls `setMaxAge`/`setDomain`.

**Fail-closed everywhere.** `serveNothing()` (`SessionHandoffServlet.java:134`)
nulls all collaborators and sets `serving=false`; init runs it on invalid
settings, absent verifier, ambiguous/unloadable provider, or any hygiene problem.
`SessionHandoffService` maps a null verifier to `DENY_ALL`; a verifier that
throws is treated as "invalid". The provider uses `ServiceLoader.stream()` +
`Provider.type()` and calls `describeProblem(candidate)` **before**
`only.get()` (`SessionStateVerifierProvider.java`), so a verifier planted in a
writable location is refused before its static initialiser or constructor runs
(the mutation battery's `SVC-hygiene-order` mutant pins this ordering).
`web.xml` maps `Throwable` to a static `error.html`, so even an `Error` yields no
stack trace to the client.

**Secret leakage / log forging (CWE-117).** The only session material ever logged
is the fingerprint; grant lines log `fingerprint` only, and errors log
`exceptionType` (`SessionHandoffServlet.handle` catch at
`SessionHandoffServlet.java:289`). `InvalidSessionIdentifierException` carries
only the rejection enum name (with `Locale.ROOT`), never the value.
`SessionId`/`SessionHandoffService` `toString()` deliberately expose only the
fingerprint/outcome. `DeploymentHygiene.logSafe`
(`DeploymentHygiene.java:101`) strips CR/LF/NUL/DEL from paths so a filename
cannot forge a second log line.

**Timing / shape oracles.** `WorkEqualizer.apply()` runs constant SHA-256 work
on every path (`SessionHandoffServlet.java:243`), before the serving check and
before the limiter, so response timing cannot rank outcomes; `ResponseBody.REFUSAL`
is byte-identical for every denial (`ResponseBody.java:19`), and GET/HEAD share
decision, headers, and work while HEAD writes no cookie (`writeBody=false`,
`SessionHandoffServlet.java:232`, `:319`). (Fixed CPU before shedding is an
accepted tradeoff: the limiter sheds the store round-trip and cookie write, not
the equaliser's fixed cost; the source reasons about this and ships a timing
harness.)

**XSS.** `ResponseBody.granted` interpolates only `escapeHtml(policy.name())`
(`ResponseBody.java:57-58`, `:67-110`). The cookie-name charset contains no HTML
metacharacters, escaping covers `& < > " '`, control characters become spaces,
and the output-width bound (`MAX_ESCAPED_LENGTH` charged against `WIDEST_ENTITY`)
makes entities whole-or-absent rather than truncated-mid-entity.

**Rate limiting (CWE-799-adjacent resource control).** `AttemptLimiter.tryAcquire`
is fully under one monitor (`AttemptLimiter.java:182`); the global ceiling is
checked *before* charging either counter (`:198-204`) so a shared-lane flood
cannot spend innocent sources' allowance; tracking is bounded
(`maxTrackedSources`) with an O(1) `RECLAIM_CANDIDATES`-sized reclaim hand so one
stalled client's scan stays independent of crowd size; the clock is monotonic;
unknown sources get a reduced ceiling.

**SSRF / resolver reach (CWE-404-adjacent).** `ClientAddress.parse` applies a
character allowlist and full dotted-quad / IPv6-literal grammar
(`ClientAddress.java:41`, `:131`, `:205-212`) **before** calling
`InetAddress.getByName` (`:222`), so inputs like `517996801`, `0x7f.1`, or a
hostname never reach the OS resolver; `::ffff:a.b.c.d` folds to /32 while the
obsoleted `::a.b.c.d` form deliberately does not fold.

**Build/provenance (dev tooling).** `build.sh` verifies the servlet-api jar
against its published SHA-1 **and** a pinned SHA-512, and the Tomcat tarball
against a pinned SHA-512, before either is used/extracted; gates stray non-ASCII
bytes and malformed `web.xml`; compiles `-Werror`; and asserts the packaged WAR
carries the four test `Stub` classes and **not** `Harness`/`E2EClient`/
`ProbeVerifier`. The unauthenticated `StubControlServlet` on `/stub/control/*`
exists only in `web.test-only.xml`, which is injected solely into throwaway test
wars and is not part of the shipped `deploy/web.xml`.

# [166] results-cyber/qwen/qwen/set_a/post_research/2/security/security_review.md
(finding headings: 10)

# Security Review: secure-data-crypto 1.0.0 (`com.example.crypto`)

## 1. Executive Summary

This is a Java 17 / Maven library that provides authenticated encryption with AES-256-GCM plus the key
handling around it: versioned key estates, four key sources (raw file, PBKDF2 container, PKCS#12
keystore, environment variable), POSIX permission enforcement for key material, and an exception type
engineered to stop secrets leaking through error paths.

The cryptographic core is sound. There are no weak or deprecated algorithms, no ECB, no static or reused
IVs, no hardcoded, default or fallback keys, keys are a fixed 256 bits, the PBKDF2 default (600,000
iterations) is at or above the current recommended floor, and the record format binds its own header into
the GCM AAD twice — once as the record claims it and once as the key/caller really has it — with no early
return that could act as a cheaper oracle than the tag check. The permission work in `PrivateFiles` is
unusually thorough for code of this kind.

Ten findings are reported. The most serious is **not** a math error but a gap in an otherwise careful
local-threat model: `KeystoreKeySource` performs the *pre-read* privacy validation for its keystore file
but skips the *post-read* inode/mode/owner re-validation that the library's own shared helper performs for
every other key file, so a local attacker who may write the keystore's parent directory can swap the file
between validation and `KeyStore.load()` (SEC-01). Second, the ownership decision that the whole
"this key file is mine" model rests on is a comparison of the `user.name` **system property** against the
file owner's name — a property any JVM launcher can set, rather than the process's real UID (SEC-02). The
remaining findings are design-level: raw key bytes are accepted with no entropy check (SEC-03), the
documented nonce-capacity limit is advice rather than an enforced ceiling (SEC-04), key material is
materialised into un-erasable `String`s in a class whose own javadoc forbids exactly that (SEC-05), and a
set of Low/informational items around lock scope, a self-documented cost oracle, RNG injection, password
length, and provider-name disclosure.

Nothing here is remotely exploitable on its own. Every finding needs either local write access to the key
storage path, a misconfigured deployment, or a caller that misuses a deliberately open extension point —
but several of them defeat controls the code claims to provide, which is the standard this review applied.

## 2. Scope

Reviewed in place, read-only, from `/data/results/qwen/set_a/post_research/2/security/`. All 14 main
sources under `src/main/java/com/example/crypto/` were read in full, together with `pom.xml` and
`README.md`; the test suite was read by targeted search. `target/` (prebuilt `secure-data-crypto-1.0.0.jar`
and compiled classes) is build output and was not opened, executed, imported or built.

| File | Purpose | Security-relevant behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| `SymmetricCrypto.java` | AES-256-GCM AEAD engine: `generateKey`, `encrypt`, `decrypt`, `decryptToString` | `AES/GCM/NoPadding`, 128-bit tag, 96-bit random nonce per record, header bound into AAD twice, `SecureRandom` injection point, documented (unenforced) nonce-capacity ceiling |
| `KeyVault.java` | Versioned key estate: active/readable/disabled versions, `rotate()`, `addReadableKey()`, per-version source cache | Routes decrypt by the record's attacker-influenceable version byte, `MAX_VERSIONS = 64` ceiling, decoy random key for unprovisioned versions so every forgery costs the same, single `rotationLock` guarding all estate mutation and cache fill |
| `PrivateFiles.java` | POSIX privacy enforcement for key material on disk | `CREATE_NEW` + `0600` at creation (no create-then-chmod window), rejects symlinks/non-regular files, owner and mode checks, ancestor-directory ownership and world-writable/sticky checks, post-read inode/mode/owner re-check when the parent is group/world-writable |
| `PasswordKeySource.java` | Passphrase-derived key from an `SPKB1` PBKDF2 container | PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256, iteration count drawn from a whitelist checked *before* any KDF work, 16-byte salt, container header as AAD, `DEFAULT_ITERATIONS = 600_000`, `char[]`/`PBEKeySpec` zeroisation, reads via the guarded `readOwnerOnlyFile` |
| `EncryptedBlob.java` | Record format and parsing | `[format][ctxFlag][keyVer][12B nonce][ct+tag]`; strict bounds before allocation; text form `v1.<base64url>[.<context>]` rejected unless it re-encodes canonically |
| `KeystoreKeySource.java` | Key from a PKCS#12 keystore entry | Store password + alias, `MAX_STORE_BYTES` and entry caps, generic failure mapping so a wrong store password is not distinguishable, `MIN_PASSPHRASE_CHARS = 32` for the entry passphrase |
| `KeyMaterial.java` | Owned 32-byte key holder with a version tag | `KEY_BYTES = 32`, zeroises on `destroy()`, `use()` zeroises its own clone, no `String` rendering |
| `CryptoException.java` | Failure type safe to hand to an untrusted audience | Four fixed user messages only, `transient` technical detail, `getCause()` returns a message-stripped stand-in, both `printStackTrace` overloads print the generic message |
| `EnvKeySource.java` | Key from a named environment variable | Variable *name* validated against a strict regex before `getenv` is called; value must decode through `KeyEncoding` |
| `KeyEncoding.java` | The two accepted key forms | Accepts exactly 32 raw bytes or canonical base64url text, `MAX_INPUT_BYTES = 4096`, canonical re-encode equality check, documented "no `String` renderer" doctrine (partly contradicted in code — SEC-05) |
| `RandomPasswords.java` | CSPRNG generation of store passphrases | `SecureRandom` over 94 printable ASCII characters, returns eraseable `char[]`, rejects out-of-range length rather than clamping |
| `KeyFileKeySource.java` | Key from a raw key file | Delegates to `PrivateFiles.readOwnerOnlyFile` (the guarded read) and `KeyEncoding.decodeKeyBytes` |
| `Limits.java` | Shared ceilings and bounds-first helper | `IV_BYTES = 12`, payload/context caps, `requirePayload` checks size before any copy or allocation |
| `KeySource.java` | Key-source SPI | `load()` / `describe()` / `release()` contract that all four sources implement |
| `pom.xml` | Build definition | JDK 17 `release` pin, single `junit-jupiter` test-scoped dependency; no runtime dependencies, no artifact checksum/verification configuration |

## 3. Skills Applied

The router skill `review-code-for-security-vulnerabilities` was loaded first and its workflow followed:
establish what the component actually does, search the sibling skill library for skills matching that
behaviour, apply the matches one at a time, then cover the residue against general OWASP Top 10 / CWE
knowledge.

* **`performing-cryptographic-audit-of-application`** — applied to `SymmetricCrypto.java`,
  `KeyEncoding.java`, `PasswordKeySource.java`, `RandomPasswords.java`, `KeyMaterial.java` and
  `KeystoreKeySource.java`: algorithm and mode selection, padding behaviour, key size, hardcoded or
  fallback keys, weak KDF parameters (iteration counts), entropy sources, and predictable IVs/nonces. This
  skill produced SEC-03 (no strength check on supplied key material), SEC-04 (nonce uniqueness guarantee),
  SEC-08 (RNG trust) and SEC-09 (generated-secret entropy), and cleared the weak-algorithm, weak-mode,
  static-IV and hardcoded-key classes entirely.
* **`implementing-aes-encryption-for-data-at-rest`** — applied to `SymmetricCrypto.encrypt/decrypt` and
  `EncryptedBlob`: never reuse a 96-bit GCM nonce under one key, generate nonces from a CSPRNG, store the
  nonce with ciphertext and tag, use ≥256-bit keys, wipe key material after use, rotate keys, and use
  ≥600,000 PBKDF2 iterations. This skill produced SEC-04 (the reuse ceiling is documented, not enforced)
  and SEC-05 (key bytes left in un-erasable heap objects), and validated the 600,000-iteration default.
* **Considered and not applicable** (matched on description, then excluded on content): envelope encryption
  with AWS KMS, secrets management with Vault, HSM/PKCS#11 key storage, RSA key-pair management, hardware
  security key authentication, API key security, Wi-Fi and hash-cat password cracking. This component has no
  KMS, no vault client, no PKCS#11, no asymmetric keys, no API keys and no cracking workflow; PKCS#12 is a
  file format, not a KMS.
* **General OWASP Top 10 / CWE knowledge** was applied to the areas the specialised skills do not cover,
  because a crypto library's real risk here is in its filesystem, concurrency and error paths: insecure
  direct object reference and path/permission handling in `PrivateFiles.java` and
  `KeystoreKeySource.java` (CWE-22, CWE-367, CWE-276, CWE-287 — SEC-01, SEC-02); error handling and
  information exposure in `CryptoException.java` (CWE-203, CWE-208, CWE-209, CWE-532 — SEC-07, SEC-10);
  concurrency and lock discipline in `KeyVault.java` (CWE-362, CWE-667, CWE-400 — SEC-06); resource
  limits and allocation-before-work ordering in `Limits.java`, `EncryptedBlob.java` and `KeyVault.java`
  (CWE-400, CWE-770 — no finding, see section 6); and secrets hygiene / clear-on-use across all key
  holders (CWE-226, CWE-316 — SEC-05).
